claims.text: The as-fabricated additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a single-phase FCC matrix.
The as-fabricated alloy has high strength and fatigue resistance.
Elevated-temperature degradation of the alloy is governed by selective oxidation and reduction of Al, Cr, and Ti.
Oxidizing exposure rapidly produces an inner Al2O3-rich layer and an outer Cr/Ti-rich oxide layer.
The proposed dual-layer oxide scale initially protects the FCC matrix.
A continuous and adherent oxide scale limits further oxidation and oxygen ingress.
Thermal stresses or phase instability can cause the protective scale to spall.
Scale spallation exposes the matrix and accelerates degradation.
Elevated-temperature phase transformation can contribute to loss of mechanical integrity.
A reducing H2-containing atmosphere suppresses formation of, or reduces, the protective oxide scale.
Suppression or reduction of the scale in a reducing atmosphere increases oxygen diffusion or internal oxidation.
Internal oxidation undermines matrix integrity and causes mechanical-property loss.
Mechanical performance will decline more rapidly in reducing gas than in oxidizing gas.
During prolonged oxidizing exposure, the initially protective scale will eventually spall and the degradation rate will increase.
The proposed mechanism is significant between 700 and 900 °C.
Degradation behavior is sensitive to gas composition.
Degradation behavior is sensitive to exposure duration.
The as-manufactured baseline has minimal surface oxidation while retaining high strength and fatigue performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome states that prolonged oxidizing exposure will eventually cause scale spallation, whereas the boundary allows that the scale may remain intact. The former is deterministic while the latter treats spallation as conditional.
